record.original_question: If k(n, R) denotes the smallest dimension of a linear code of length n and covering radius R, is it always true for R ≠ n that k(n + 2, R + 1) ≤ k(n, R)?

evidence.quote: The smallest dimension of a linear code of length n and covering radius R is denoted by k(n, R).
Open Question 12.4. Is k(n + 2, R + 1) ≤ k(n, R) for all R ≠ n?[18].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $n$ and $R$ with $0 \le R \le n$, let $k(n, R)$ denote the smallest dimension $k$ such that there exists a linear code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ of length $n$, dimension $k$, and covering radius exactly $R$ (i.e., every vector of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ lies within Hamming distance $R$ of some codeword of $C$, and $R$ is the least such integer). 

Determine whether the inequality
$$k(n+2,\, R+1) \;\le\; k(n, R)$$
holds for every pair $(n, R)$ with $R \ne n$.
artifact.status_search_result: A related inequality for the minimum cardinality K(n,R) of (not necessarily linear) covering codes is known to hold for sufficiently large n, but no source found explicitly resolves the linear-dimension version k(n+2,R+1) ≤ k(n,R) for all (n,R) with R ≠ n. The status appears unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Covering Radius — Survey and Recent Results
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys bounds on k(n,R) and K(n,R) for covering codes; lists monotonicity-type inequalities as part of ongoing study.
status_evidence.claim: Standard surveys present k(n,R) bounds without resolving the specific monotonicity inequality k(n+2,R+1) ≤ k(n,R) for all R ≠ n.

status_evidence.title: Linear codes with covering radius 2 and other new covering codes
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses bounds and constructions for linear covering codes of small covering radius.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial results but does not establish the full monotonicity claim.
